$comment: [X4.16] Chroma (ChromaDB) MCP attach spec. Tier-2 VERIFIED-PUBLISHER (publisher `chroma-core` — official Chroma MCP server from github.com/chroma-core/chroma-mcp; promoted community→verified-publisher in X4.16). Shape === mcp-specs/_template.json (X2.1). Embedding-database collections + semantic/full-text retrieval. First Tier-2 spec with declared destructive tools. CC0-1.0.
title: Chroma Embedding Database
description: Create collections and run semantic, full-text, and metadata search over the Chroma embedding database via the official Chroma MCP server.

env_vars.name: CHROMA_CLIENT_TYPE
env_vars.description: Client backend: ephemeral (in-memory, default), persistent (file-based), http (self-hosted), or cloud (Chroma Cloud).

env_vars.name: CHROMA_DATA_DIR
env_vars.description: Directory for the persistent client's on-disk storage.

env_vars.name: CHROMA_API_KEY
env_vars.description: API key for Chroma Cloud (api.trychroma.com). Pass via env, never inline in args (doctrine #6).

env_vars.name: CHROMA_HOST
env_vars.description: Host of a self-hosted Chroma instance (http client).

env_vars.name: CHROMA_PORT
env_vars.description: Port of a self-hosted Chroma instance (http client).

auth.recipe: default ephemeral/persistent clients need no auth; for Chroma Cloud set CHROMA_CLIENT_TYPE=cloud with CHROMA_API_KEY + CHROMA_TENANT + CHROMA_DATABASE.

sample_tools.name: chroma_list_collections
sample_tools.summary: List all collections with pagination support.

sample_tools.name: chroma_create_collection
sample_tools.summary: Create a new collection with optional HNSW configuration.

sample_tools.name: chroma_add_documents
sample_tools.summary: Add documents with optional metadata and custom IDs.

sample_tools.name: chroma_query_documents
sample_tools.summary: Query documents using semantic search with advanced filtering.

sample_tools.name: chroma_get_documents
sample_tools.summary: Retrieve documents by IDs or filters with pagination.

sample_tools.name: chroma_delete_collection
sample_tools.summary: Delete a collection and all of its documents.

sample_tools.name: chroma_delete_documents
sample_tools.summary: Delete specific documents from a collection.

known_limitations: Runs via `uvx chroma-mcp`, so the host needs uv / Python available on PATH; the package is fetched and installed on first launch.

A client type must be chosen: ephemeral is in-memory and lost on exit; persistent needs CHROMA_DATA_DIR; self-hosted http needs CHROMA_HOST/CHROMA_PORT; Chroma Cloud needs a CHROMA_API_KEY credential plus CHROMA_TENANT + CHROMA_DATABASE.

Each collection persists its embedding function (default local model, or external cohere/openai/jina/voyageai providers requiring a CHROMA_<PROVIDER>_API_KEY); collections created on Chroma <=0.6.3 do not persist the embedding function.

Destructive-action audit (X2.18): chroma_delete_collection and chroma_delete_documents are destructive (declared in destructive_tools) and confirm per call under the verified-publisher policy; chroma_modify_collection / chroma_update_documents mutate in place but are not delete-class.

client_install.claude_desktop: Add to claude_desktop_config.json mcpServers as `chroma`: { command: uvx, args: [chroma-mcp] } (ephemeral), or append --client-type persistent --data-dir <path>.
client_install.cursor: Settings → MCP → Add: name `chroma`, command `uvx chroma-mcp`; configure the client type via CHROMA_CLIENT_TYPE in the env.
client_install.vscode: Add to .vscode/mcp.json servers as `chroma` with command `uvx chroma-mcp`; supply CHROMA_API_KEY via inputs for the cloud client.
